title: Business Growth Glossary: Key Terms Explained | GOP
description: Plain-language definitions of EBITDA, working capital, investment readiness, value-creation plans, due diligence and other growth terms.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Profitable Growth
hasDefinedTerm.description: Revenue growth that also raises profit, cash and the quality of earnings, rather than growth bought with deeper discounts, longer credit or rising cost.

hasDefinedTerm.name: EBITDA
hasDefinedTerm.description: Earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation: operating profit before financing costs and non-cash charges.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Working Capital
hasDefinedTerm.description: The money tied up in running the business day to day: inventory plus receivables minus payables.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Commercial Excellence
hasDefinedTerm.description: The discipline of earning the most from the business you already have: pricing, discount control, key-account management and an effective sales process.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Customer Acquisition Cost
hasDefinedTerm.description: The total sales and marketing spend needed to win one new customer, over a defined period.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Customer Lifetime Value
hasDefinedTerm.description: The total margin a customer is expected to contribute over the whole relationship, not just the first order.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Gross Margin
hasDefinedTerm.description: Revenue minus the direct cost of the goods sold, as a share of revenue.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Operating Leverage
hasDefinedTerm.description: The degree to which profit grows faster than revenue because part of the cost base is fixed.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Investment Readiness
hasDefinedTerm.description: The state in which an outside investor can trust a business's numbers, people, governance and plan without relying on the promoter's memory.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Value-Creation Plan
hasDefinedTerm.description: A prioritised, owned and measured set of initiatives that turns an investment thesis into operating results.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Portfolio Company
hasDefinedTerm.description: A business in which a private equity or venture capital fund has invested.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Due Diligence
hasDefinedTerm.description: The investigation an investor or acquirer carries out before committing capital, covering financial, commercial, operational, legal and tax matters.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Capital Allocation
hasDefinedTerm.description: How a business decides where to spend its money: capacity, working capital, new markets, debt reduction or returns to owners.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Governance
hasDefinedTerm.description: The structures and routines that decide who can decide what: board calendar, committees, delegation of authority and approval limits.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Management Reporting
hasDefinedTerm.description: The regular pack of operating and financial information leadership uses to run the business, often called MIS.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Market Expansion
hasDefinedTerm.description: Growing into new customer segments, products, categories, channels or geographies.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Sales Productivity
hasDefinedTerm.description: The revenue or margin produced per unit of sales effort, such as per salesperson, per call or per rupee of sales cost.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Post-Investment Value Creation
hasDefinedTerm.description: The work done after capital arrives to deliver the growth, margin and capability changes the investment assumed.
